service_at_issue: SNF occupational therapy furnished to one beneficiary (J.M.), Aug 1-31, 2009
facts: Beneficiary J.M. Dates of Service: August 1, 2009 to August 31, 2009

Initially and at redetermination, the Medicare contractor determined that the SNF services provided were not medically reasonable and necessary. On reconsideration, the Qualified Independent Contractor (QIC) also determined the services were not medically reasonable and necessary. See J.M. Exh. 1 at 2-7.
The appellant contends that the record shows sufficient evidence that J.M.’s physician was aware, ordered, and was in agreement with the therapy plans. See id.
The certification and recertification statements may be entered on forms, notes, or records that the appropriate individual signs, or on a special separate form.

Regarding OT, services were initiated on June 14, 2009, with a treatment diagnosis of muscle weakness. Repetitive strengthening exercises were provided, yet the record does not indicate that significant functional gains occurred. As noted by the QIC, sufficient time had passed to establish a restorative program with nursing staff for ongoing strengthening exercises and verbal cueing.
